findings.title: Goal authorization remains gateway-authoritative and fail-closed
findings.detail: Each managed implementation turn and bounded delivery cycle re-fetches canonical Goal execution state, inherits the exact approved proposal, and checks the shared execution window and aggregate requested consumption through GameApi.Client; malformed managed identity/projection, missing gateway contract, provider errors, and invalid gateway decisions prevent work from starting.

findings.title: Single-decision scope and budget boundaries are preserved
findings.detail: Included work is restricted to includedIssueNumbers, derived repair requires strictly_derived policy, pending scope changes and closed windows pause, 75 percent consumption exposes scope_frozen, and exhausted or over-requested aggregate ceilings stop new work without local budget replenishment.

findings.title: Repair orchestration is bounded and exact-commit evidence is affirmative
findings.detail: The default specialist repair limit is reduced from three to two cycles. Local HEAD and remote bos/issue-53 both equal aed939a508bf0ae1aca96532bf35a39dc3254b19; exact-commit evidence reports formatting, git diff checks, 385 tests with 0 failures and 2 skipped, and 11 focused Goal execution tests with 0 failures.

summary: Passed: the exact commit implements gateway-owned single-Goal authorization, fail-closed managed identity and projection handling, shared execution-window and aggregate-budget enforcement, restart-safe rechecks, and a two-cycle repair bound; local and remote candidate SHAs match and exact-commit validation evidence is affirmative.
